The Layout Disappears

Because your routes are siblings, not parent/child.

lightbulb

Why is this happening?

In your code, /Test is a sibling to the layout route. When React Router matches /Test, it unmounts the Layout entirely to show ExampleComponent.

To fix this, you must nest the routes. Make Layout the parent, and place Home and ExampleComponent inside it. You also need to add an <Outlet /> to your Layout component.

App.js
info Notice how the routes are separate siblings.

Rendering: Layout Route
account_tree

1. Nesting is Key

In React Router v6, if you want a component (like a Layout) to stay visible while its content changes, it must be a Parent Route.

<Route element={<Layout />}>
  <Route path="child" ... />
</Route>
input

2. The <Outlet />

The parent component (Layout) doesn't know where to put the child content automatically. You must render the <Outlet /> component inside it.

// Inside Layout.js
return (
  <div>
    <Navbar />
    <Outlet />
  </div>
)

Final Solution Code

App.js 
import React from 'react';
import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route } from 'react-router-dom';
import ExampleComponent from './components/ExampleComponent';
import Layout from "./components/Layout";
import Home from './Home';

function App() {
  return (
    <BrowserRouter>
      <Routes>
        {/* Layout is now the parent route */}
        <Route path="/" element={<Layout />}>
          
          {/* Child routes render inside Layout's Outlet */}
          <Route index element={<Home />} />
          <Route path="Test" element={<ExampleComponent />} />
          
        </Route>
      </Routes>
    </BrowserRouter>
  );
}

export default App;

And don't forget Layout.js!

Ensure your layout component renders the outlet.

import { Outlet } from 'react-router-dom';

// ... inside your component ...
<Content>
   <Outlet />
</Content>
